title: Ye Sons of Pride, That Hate the Just
description: Ye Sons of Pride, That Hate the Just in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 49, part 2, headed “Death and the resurrection”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ye sons of pride, that hate the just, And tram-ple on the poor, When death has brought you down to dust, Your pomp shall rise no more,

lines: Ye sons of pride, that hate the just,
When death has brought you down to dust,
Your pomp shall rise no more,
The last great day shall change the scene;
When shall the just revive, and reign
O'er all that scorn'd them here?
God will my naked soul receive,
And break the prison of the grave
Let men of pride their rage resume,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
